` [Highlight start] Feeling depressed after drinking is common and happens because alcohol acts as a central nervous system depressant that disrupts brain chemistry and sleep [Highlight end] ` . While alcohol may temporarily boost mood or relaxation while you drink, low mood, sadness, or anxiety ("hangxiety") often follow as it wears off.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14Hgx9egwsIlZM0ynu2AI-iAIntgDwuhokW4GYMkvTgqicQlzo7f0SI-ST7yaBacIcoaHw0iclRIJMv7V7ZdMBA2HSziAOY_vrRy9ecA1SXuz_6sfoLNziVh83JuLKi18jty-htbdZeEP-GNrtpPVYi-oqaBHsXIqm40adOipUY)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXBJZr-Lf_R-KJGPV7h5fn5ShBwQtl_Dhn55VLEqoV6SAYkBqC4a-Fa9ROnnzOfjJYftdheENiiWdASi3vmUhY_eloGM-dIRlQ0MI7BeVBTzBYYFHWTC9aDBPbObKX4kHKTVUnXIA6sqTgSi_8uKA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXh0XDrEpWw1ioYo6qAzwLIyBprjThDprLupaYWNQF-mZgrTGFxi_VmTDv2cco7eQfehoUPp_-lu588zYqHFtuBweS6siiwAKsA1vXO3QXtZujsAxJfx9wPz7qDkeM_N5zI0t1N-dFB0kwBAVhKP8MDQG0-yUDrw)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF1-HiUpTHCGg5QmjAopbKiFx4ILFuUEyXb03m3J5WVs01kKbVOazU3caJxeguYx-KbzOXu6FTZ9A1maoxqGGDt_Fyv2Fu4yDHJz0coaVM15x2bs3CQU8BNt53JHHA923CcDloDMkT9lfWbLB0CLVcqXTtt1qAs4Av65M43ayzNPb2k1bsMcVOUTBX9Rp7IvgPEQ)

### Why It Happens

- **Brain chemistry shifts:** Alcohol temporarily alters neurotransmitters like dopamine and serotonin. Once it clears, levels can dip or rebalance unevenly, leaving you feeling low or anxious. Most users on [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xZPa-Jl_j5TN_9Fis9SG2I17wgSknMMhmoJ9I0wWtIdYFL5tHB-aMrGo0L6DZv0ICJIOop_iX8qN8w_0S1qZeFaynZNTfkAR0dGCFN__YJCL4D2FWYc00aQAJ4EFvM8T7cP6ZCUGPRXmVekuv9vaEnQ7xLGfcAPem5DrxpQjKF7v3QQ-NxmuxH5zBqPw7cBH5da_UNU2d6BGnTpBQ) agree that this post-drinking dopamine drop is a major driver of next-day low mood, especially for people with underlying dopamine regulation differences like ADHD.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xZPa-Jl_j5TN_9Fis9SG2I17wgSknMMhmoJ9I0wWtIdYFL5tHB-aMrGo0L6DZv0ICJIOop_iX8qN8w_0S1qZeFaynZNTfkAR0dGCFN__YJCL4D2FWYc00aQAJ4EFvM8T7cP6ZCUGPRXmVekuv9vaEnQ7xLGfcAPem5DrxpQjKF7v3QQ-NxmuxH5zBqPw7cBH5da_UNU2d6BGnTpBQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXBJZr-Lf_R-KJGPV7h5fn5ShBwQtl_Dhn55VLEqoV6SAYkBqC4a-Fa9ROnnzOfjJYftdheENiiWdASi3vmUhY_eloGM-dIRlQ0MI7BeVBTzBYYFHWTC9aDBPbObKX4kHKTVUnXIA6sqTgSi_8uKA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXh0XDrEpWw1ioYo6qAzwLIyBprjThDprLupaYWNQF-mZgrTGFxi_VmTDv2cco7eQfehoUPp_-lu588zYqHFtuBweS6siiwAKsA1vXO3QXtZujsAxJfx9wPz7qDkeM_N5zI0t1N-dFB0kwBAVhKP8MDQG0-yUDrw)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF1-HiUpTHCGg5QmjAopbKiFx4ILFuUEyXb03m3J5WVs01kKbVOazU3caJxeguYx-KbzOXu6FTZ9A1maoxqGGDt_Fyv2Fu4yDHJz0coaVM15x2bs3CQU8BNt53JHHA923CcDloDMkT9lfWbLB0CLVcqXTtt1qAs4Av65M43ayzNPb2k1bsMcVOUTBX9Rp7IvgPEQ)
- **Poor sleep:** Drinking can make you fall asleep faster, but it disrupts restorative sleep cycles, which worsens mood the next day.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXBJZr-Lf_R-KJGPV7h5fn5ShBwQtl_Dhn55VLEqoV6SAYkBqC4a-Fa9ROnnzOfjJYftdheENiiWdASi3vmUhY_eloGM-dIRlQ0MI7BeVBTzBYYFHWTC9aDBPbObKX4kHKTVUnXIA6sqTgSi_8uKA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXh0XDrEpWw1ioYo6qAzwLIyBprjThDprLupaYWNQF-mZgrTGFxi_VmTDv2cco7eQfehoUPp_-lu588zYqHFtuBweS6siiwAKsA1vXO3QXtZujsAxJfx9wPz7qDkeM_N5zI0t1N-dFB0kwBAVhKP8MDQG0-yUDrw)
- **Physical and emotional factors:** Dehydration, low blood sugar, lowered inhibitions, or regret over actions while drinking can add to feelings of sadness or dread.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF1-HiUpTHCGg5QmjAopbKiFx4ILFuUEyXb03m3J5WVs01kKbVOazU3caJxeguYx-KbzOXu6FTZ9A1maoxqGGDt_Fyv2Fu4yDHJz0coaVM15x2bs3CQU8BNt53JHHA923CcDloDMkT9lfWbLB0CLVcqXTtt1qAs4Av65M43ayzNPb2k1bsMcVOUTBX9Rp7IvgPEQ)
- **Underlying mood or drinking patterns:** Heavy or regular drinking—or using alcohol to cope with stress or sadness—can intensify depressive symptoms over time.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXPVZyBziIYYrbNkB8lHX7mme3cYuMujXua_m42suyfDifxVNgHOkbRg9mKeKwN9BVWvjPv0CdJtxl59RSgaL1-SCZ1GovAFCJNI9-GgUnekc7uybMM-FeBsjNPYBztciAdXB-8ZWMXw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXBJZr-Lf_R-KJGPV7h5fn5ShBwQtl_Dhn55VLEqoV6SAYkBqC4a-Fa9ROnnzOfjJYftdheENiiWdASi3vmUhY_eloGM-dIRlQ0MI7BeVBTzBYYFHWTC9aDBPbObKX4kHKTVUnXIA6sqTgSi_8uKA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14Hgx9egwsIlZM0ynu2AI-iAIntgDwuhokW4GYMkvTgqicQlzo7f0SI-ST7yaBacIcoaHw0iclRIJMv7V7ZdMBA2HSziAOY_vrRy9ecA1SXuz_6sfoLNziVh83JuLKi18jty-htbdZeEP-GNrtpPVYi-oqaBHsXIqm40adOipUY)

### Ways to Cope and Prevent It

- **Care for your body after drinking:** Hydrate with water, eat a balanced meal, rest, and try gentle movement like a short walk.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXh0XDrEpWw1ioYo6qAzwLIyBprjThDprLupaYWNQF-mZgrTGFxi_VmTDv2cco7eQfehoUPp_-lu588zYqHFtuBweS6siiwAKsA1vXO3QXtZujsAxJfx9wPz7qDkeM_N5zI0t1N-dFB0kwBAVhKP8MDQG0-yUDrw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXBJZr-Lf_R-KJGPV7h5fn5ShBwQtl_Dhn55VLEqoV6SAYkBqC4a-Fa9ROnnzOfjJYftdheENiiWdASi3vmUhY_eloGM-dIRlQ0MI7BeVBTzBYYFHWTC9aDBPbObKX4kHKTVUnXIA6sqTgSi_8uKA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14Hgx9egwsIlZM0ynu2AI-iAIntgDwuhokW4GYMkvTgqicQlzo7f0SI-ST7yaBacIcoaHw0iclRIJMv7V7ZdMBA2HSziAOY_vrRy9ecA1SXuz_6sfoLNziVh83JuLKi18jty-htbdZeEP-GNrtpPVYi-oqaBHsXIqm40adOipUY)
- **Avoid self-blame:** Remind yourself that post-drinking low mood is often a temporary chemical rebound rather than a permanent state.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14Hgx9egwsIlZM0ynu2AI-iAIntgDwuhokW4GYMkvTgqicQlzo7f0SI-ST7yaBacIcoaHw0iclRIJMv7V7ZdMBA2HSziAOY_vrRy9ecA1SXuz_6sfoLNziVh83JuLKi18jty-htbdZeEP-GNrtpPVYi-oqaBHsXIqm40adOipUY)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF1-HiUpTHCGg5QmjAopbKiFx4ILFuUEyXb03m3J5WVs01kKbVOazU3caJxeguYx-KbzOXu6FTZ9A1maoxqGGDt_Fyv2Fu4yDHJz0coaVM15x2bs3CQU8BNt53JHHA923CcDloDMkT9lfWbLB0CLVcqXTtt1qAs4Av65M43ayzNPb2k1bsMcVOUTBX9Rp7IvgPEQ)
- **Pace or cut back:** Drink more slowly, space drinks with water or alcohol-free options, eat before drinking, or take breaks from alcohol to see how your mood responds.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14Hgx9egwsIlZM0ynu2AI-iAIntgDwuhokW4GYMkvTgqicQlzo7f0SI-ST7yaBacIcoaHw0iclRIJMv7V7ZdMBA2HSziAOY_vrRy9ecA1SXuz_6sfoLNziVh83JuLKi18jty-htbdZeEP-GNrtpPVYi-oqaBHsXIqm40adOipUY)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXBJZr-Lf_R-KJGPV7h5fn5ShBwQtl_Dhn55VLEqoV6SAYkBqC4a-Fa9ROnnzOfjJYftdheENiiWdASi3vmUhY_eloGM-dIRlQ0MI7BeVBTzBYYFHWTC9aDBPbObKX4kHKTVUnXIA6sqTgSi_8uKA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXh0XDrEpWw1ioYo6qAzwLIyBprjThDprLupaYWNQF-mZgrTGFxi_VmTDv2cco7eQfehoUPp_-lu588zYqHFtuBweS6siiwAKsA1vXO3QXtZujsAxJfx9wPz7qDkeM_N5zI0t1N-dFB0kwBAVhKP8MDQG0-yUDrw)
- **Build non-alcohol coping habits:** Use exercise, mindfulness, journaling, or talking with friends or a therapist to handle stress or low moods.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14Hgx9egwsIlZM0ynu2AI-iAIntgDwuhokW4GYMkvTgqicQlzo7f0SI-ST7yaBacIcoaHw0iclRIJMv7V7ZdMBA2HSziAOY_vrRy9ecA1SXuz_6sfoLNziVh83JuLKi18jty-htbdZeEP-GNrtpPVYi-oqaBHsXIqm40adOipUY)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXBJZr-Lf_R-KJGPV7h5fn5ShBwQtl_Dhn55VLEqoV6SAYkBqC4a-Fa9ROnnzOfjJYftdheENiiWdASi3vmUhY_eloGM-dIRlQ0MI7BeVBTzBYYFHWTC9aDBPbObKX4kHKTVUnXIA6sqTgSi_8uKA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXh0XDrEpWw1ioYo6qAzwLIyBprjThDprLupaYWNQF-mZgrTGFxi_VmTDv2cco7eQfehoUPp_-lu588zYqHFtuBweS6siiwAKsA1vXO3QXtZujsAxJfx9wPz7qDkeM_N5zI0t1N-dFB0kwBAVhKP8MDQG0-yUDrw)

[Healthline](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14Hgx9egwsIlZM0ynu2AI-iAIntgDwuhokW4GYMkvTgqicQlzo7f0SI-ST7yaBacIcoaHw0iclRIJMv7V7ZdMBA2HSziAOY_vrRy9ecA1SXuz_6sfoLNziVh83JuLKi18jty-htbdZeEP-GNrtpPVYi-oqaBHsXIqm40adOipUY) and [Lemonade Health](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXBJZr-Lf_R-KJGPV7h5fn5ShBwQtl_Dhn55VLEqoV6SAYkBqC4a-Fa9ROnnzOfjJYftdheENiiWdASi3vmUhY_eloGM-dIRlQ0MI7BeVBTzBYYFHWTC9aDBPbObKX4kHKTVUnXIA6sqTgSi_8uKA) offer more detail on how alcohol affects mood and practical steps for managing hangover depression.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14Hgx9egwsIlZM0ynu2AI-iAIntgDwuhokW4GYMkvTgqicQlzo7f0SI-ST7yaBacIcoaHw0iclRIJMv7V7ZdMBA2HSziAOY_vrRy9ecA1SXuz_6sfoLNziVh83JuLKi18jty-htbdZeEP-GNrtpPVYi-oqaBHsXIqm40adOipUY)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXBJZr-Lf_R-KJGPV7h5fn5ShBwQtl_Dhn55VLEqoV6SAYkBqC4a-Fa9ROnnzOfjJYftdheENiiWdASi3vmUhY_eloGM-dIRlQ0MI7BeVBTzBYYFHWTC9aDBPbObKX4kHKTVUnXIA6sqTgSi_8uKA)

### When to Seek Support
If low mood lasts more than a couple of days, happens frequently, or makes it hard to cut back on drinking, consider talking with a healthcare provider or counselor. You can also find confidential support and treatment resources through [SAMHSA](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESUgHEIkXXfmdBVLTaaQj3-bSBOQi97p904TuK3wgkT75iqqfPLvunXhyER1vk8-GPcZkXN21XZLCFDg1efAuQkYj5yf9UQ1SAhTHYUR6JFsiV_TU) (or call/text **988** in the US if you are in crisis).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14Hgx9egwsIlZM0ynu2AI-iAIntgDwuhokW4GYMkvTgqicQlzo7f0SI-ST7yaBacIcoaHw0iclRIJMv7V7ZdMBA2HSziAOY_vrRy9ecA1SXuz_6sfoLNziVh83JuLKi18jty-htbdZeEP-GNrtpPVYi-oqaBHsXIqm40adOipUY)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXPVZyBziIYYrbNkB8lHX7mme3cYuMujXua_m42suyfDifxVNgHOkbRg9mKeKwN9BVWvjPv0CdJtxl59RSgaL1-SCZ1GovAFCJNI9-GgUnekc7uybMM-FeBsjNPYBztciAdXB-8ZWMXw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXh0XDrEpWw1ioYo6qAzwLIyBprjThDprLupaYWNQF-mZgrTGFxi_VmTDv2cco7eQfehoUPp_-lu588zYqHFtuBweS6siiwAKsA1vXO3QXtZujsAxJfx9wPz7qDkeM_N5zI0t1N-dFB0kwBAVhKP8MDQG0-yUDrw)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESUgHEIkXXfmdBVLTaaQj3-bSBOQi97p904TuK3wgkT75iqqfPLvunXhyER1vk8-GPcZkXN21XZLCFDg1efAuQkYj5yf9UQ1SAhTHYUR6JFsiV_TU)

Most users on Reddit agree that this post-drinking dopamine drop is a major driver of next-day low mood, especially for people with underlying dopamine regulation differences like ADHD. Poor sleep: Drinking can make you fall asleep faster, but it disrupts restorative sleep cycles, which worsens mood the next day. Physical and emotional factors: Dehydration, low blood sugar, lowered inhibitions, or regret over actions while drinking can add to feelings of sadness or dread. Underlying mood or drinking patterns: Heavy or regular drinking—or using alcohol to cope with stress or sadness—can intensify depressive symptoms over time.

- **Underlying mood or drinking patterns:** Heavy or regular drinking—or using alcohol to cope with stress or sadness—can intensify depressive symptoms over time.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXPVZyBziIYYrbNkB8lHX7mme3cYuMujXua_m42suyfDifxVNgHOkbRg9mKeKwN9BVWvjPv0CdJtxl59RSgaL1-SCZ1GovAFCJNI9-GgUnekc7uybMM-FeBsjNPYBztciAdXB-8ZWMXw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXBJZr-Lf_R-KJGPV7h5fn5ShBwQtl_Dhn55VLEqoV6SAYkBqC4a-Fa9ROnnzOfjJYftdheENiiWdASi3vmUhY_eloGM-dIRlQ0MI7BeVBTzBYYFHWTC9aDBPbObKX4kHKTVUnXIA6sqTgSi_8uKA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14Hgx9egwsIlZM0ynu2AI-iAIntgDwuhokW4GYMkvTgqicQlzo7f0SI-ST7yaBacIcoaHw0iclRIJMv7V7ZdMBA2HSziAOY_vrRy9ecA1SXuz_6sfoLNziVh83JuLKi18jty-htbdZeEP-GNrtpPVYi-oqaBHsXIqm40adOipUY)

items.title: Ways to Cope and Prevent It
items.text: Care for your body after drinking: Hydrate with water, eat a balanced meal, rest, and try gentle movement like a short walk. Avoid self-blame: Remind yourself that post-drinking low mood is often a temporary chemical rebound rather than a permanent state. Pace or cut back: Drink more slowly, space drinks with water or alcohol-free options, eat before drinking, or take breaks from alcohol to see how your mood responds. Build non-alcohol coping habits: Use exercise, mindfulness, journaling, or talking with friends or a therapist to handle stress or low moods.

items.title: When to Seek Support
items.text: If low mood lasts more than a couple of days, happens frequently, or makes it hard to cut back on drinking, consider talking with a healthcare provider or counselor. You can also find confidential support and treatment resources through SAMHSA (or call/text 988 in the US if you are in crisis).
